# Energy and Its Units — chapter overview blocks

::: overview ch01
answers: What is energy, what forms does it take, and in which units is it measured? [p.1: "This chapter introduces the main forms of energy and the units used to measure it."]
big-picture: Every chemical and physical change involves energy; Chapter 2 applies these ideas to the heat that flows during those changes. [p.1: "Every chemical and physical change involves energy."] [p.6: "This chapter applies those ideas to the heat that flows during chemical and physical changes"]
:::

::: must-know ch01
point: Energy is the capacity to supply heat or do work. [p.1: "Energy is the capacity to supply heat or do work."] (covers: SUM-ch01-1)
point: Kinetic energy is energy of motion; potential energy is energy of position, composition, or condition. [p.5: "Kinetic energy is energy of motion, and potential energy is energy of position, composition, or condition."] (covers: SUM-ch01-2)
point: Because speed is squared in KE = ½mv², doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy four times larger. [p.1: "Because the speed is squared, doubling the speed of an object multiplies its kinetic energy by four."]
point: Thermal energy is the kinetic energy of randomly moving atoms and molecules. [p.5: "Thermal energy is the kinetic energy of randomly moving particles."] (covers: SUM-ch01-3)
point: Energy changes form but is never created or destroyed. [p.2: "Energy can be converted from one form to another, but it is never created or destroyed."]
point: The joule (J) is the SI unit of energy, and 1 kJ = 1000 J. [p.3: "The SI unit of energy is the joule (J)."] [p.3: "so chemists often report energies in kilojoules (kJ); 1 kJ = 1000 J"] (covers: SUM-ch01-4)
point: One calorie is exactly 4.184 joules, and a food Calorie is 1000 cal. [p.3: "1 cal = 4.184 J (exactly)"] [p.4: "1 Calorie = 1 kcal = 1000 cal."] (covers: SUM-ch01-5)
:::

::: compare CMP-ch01-01
items: T-kinetic-energy | T-potential-energy
row: Comes from | the object's motion [p.1: "Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its motion."] | the object's position, composition, or condition [p.2: "Potential energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its position, composition, or condition."]
row: Example | a rolling ball or a flowing river [p.1: "A rolling ball, a flowing river, and a vibrating molecule all have kinetic energy."] | a ball held above the ground, or a battery [p.2: "A ball held above the ground has gravitational potential energy, and a battery stores chemical potential energy in the arrangement of its atoms."]
row: Ball on a hill | grows as the ball rolls down [p.2: "As it rolls down, potential energy is converted to kinetic energy."] | largest at the top of the hill [p.2: "A ball at the top of a hill has maximum potential energy."]
:::

::: compare CMP-ch01-02
items: T-kinetic-energy | T-thermal-energy
row: What moves | a whole object, such as a rolling ball [p.1: "A rolling ball, a flowing river, and a vibrating molecule all have kinetic energy."] | the atoms and molecules inside matter, at random [p.2: "The atoms and molecules in any sample of matter are in constant random motion."]
row: How they relate | energy of motion in general [p.1: "Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its motion."] | one kind of kinetic energy: that of randomly moving particles [p.2: "Thermal energy is the kinetic energy associated with the random motion of these particles."]
:::

::: strategy ch01
row: The question gives a mass and a speed and asks for energy | use KE = ½mv², with mass in kilograms and speed in meters per second [p.1: "where m is the mass of the object in kilograms and v is its speed in meters per second"]
row: The question gives energy in calories and asks for joules | multiply by 4.184 J per calorie [p.3: "1 cal = 4.184 J (exactly)"]
row: The question uses food Calories (capital C) | first convert, because 1 Calorie = 1000 cal [p.4: "1 Calorie = 1 kcal = 1000 cal."]
:::
